items.title: Lifecycle guard and invalid-state behavior is unspecified
items.statement: The nominal lifecycle is named, but the core does not define guards or outcomes for requests before initialized, duplicate initialize, shutdown with in-flight work, exit without shutdown, late responses, cancellation races, or server death during a transition.
items.impact: Protocol violations can leak requests, hang shutdown, or apply stale responses after a session is no longer authoritative.

items.impact: A server or component failure can leave diagnostics and request state stale while appearing usable.

items.title: Rejected OpenCode behavior lacks enforceable thresholds
items.statement: LSPS-014 rejects uncontrolled downloads, duplicate processes, weak status visibility, and unbounded backoff, but defines no download authorization rule, deduplication invariant, backoff ceiling, eviction trigger, or status-state oracle.
items.impact: Builders can claim compliance while retaining unsafe downloads, duplicated processes, indefinite retry, or misleading status.

items.statement: Custom server definitions, environment and initialization options, diagnostics, completion content, workspace edits, and Slint live preview all cross trust boundaries, yet the core gives no executable provenance checks, command allowlist, environment filtering, payload-size validation, URI/path confinement, markup sanitization, or preview isolation contract.
items.impact: A malicious workspace or server can execute an unexpected binary, exfiltrate environment data, escape workspace paths, exhaust resources, or inject unsafe rendered content.

dimension_assessments.summary: Callers, consumers, and ordering are not encoded despite many named integration surfaces.
Nominal lifecycle order exists, but invalid and interrupted transition semantics are absent.
Request cancellation, late response, duplicate spawn, and root-identity races lack contracts.
Component, process, and handshake partial failures have no specified disposition.
Restart, resync, retry, quarantine, and edit rollback behavior is not specified.
Capability restraint is explicit, but adjacent subsystem precedence and enforcement remain undefined.
Assistant-bound diagnostics lack consent, minimization, redaction, retention, and deletion rules.
Custom binaries, options, payloads, edits, and preview content lack trust and validation boundaries.
User-visible availability, freshness, degradation, and restart-required states are absent.
Missing binary, installation consent, registry outage, and network-loss behavior is unspecified.
No resource, queue, process, payload, trace, or timing ceilings are stated.
No keyboard, focus, announcement, contrast, reduced-motion, or non-color requirements exist for GUI-related units.
User-facing LSP state, settings, diagnostics, and locale propagation have no localization contract.
Toolchain, configuration, protocol, persisted-setting, and client-stack migration rules are incomplete.
Named trace and telemetry surfaces lack schemas, correlation, redaction, retention, health thresholds, and support export.
FileSafe routing is an explicit non-gap, but confirmation, atomicity, conflict, undo, and rollback semantics remain absent.
Owner boundaries and ContractRefs are traceable but their interface contracts and conflict rules are not.
Acceptance and validation surfaces test preservation and indexing, not the stated runtime properties.
The selected async client stack and its current viability cannot be determined from the blind excerpt; external research is intentionally deferred.
